explain.ja: 相手の駒がいる場所に動かせば駒を取れ、相手の戦力を減らせます。駒台の持ち駒は常に相手に見えるように置き、隠し持つのは「隠し駒」というマナー違反です。相手から取った駒が成駒でも、自分の駒台に置くときは裏返して生駒に戻します。たとえば図ではと金を取っていますが、駒台には表の歩兵として置きます。
explain.en: Moving onto an opponent's piece captures it and reduces their force. Pieces in hand must always be visible to the opponent; hiding them is bad manners called "hidden pieces" (隠し駒). Even if the captured piece was promoted, it is flipped back to its unpromoted side when placed on your komadai; in the figure the captured tokin goes onto the stand as a pawn.

section.ja: 駒の取り方の基本、相手の駒がいるマスに動こう!
section.en: Basics of capturing: move onto the square holding the opponent's piece!

label.ja: 相手の駒があるマスへ…
label.en: Move onto a square holding an enemy piece…
…capture it and put it on your stand

title.ja: 成駒を取っても表に戻す
title.en: A captured promoted piece returns to its front side

explain.ja: 持駒は自分の手番に盤上の好きなマスに置けますが、1枚置けば手番は終わりなので、駒を動かすことはできません。置けるのは他の駒がいないマスだけです。たとえば図では、持ち駒の角行は青く塗ったマスのどこにでも置けます。
explain.en: On your turn you can drop a piece in hand on any square, but dropping one ends your turn, so you cannot also move a piece. You may only drop on empty squares; in the figure, the bishop in hand can go on any of the blue squares.

section.ja: 成駒を取っても、表に戻す
section.en: Even when you capture a promoted piece, turn it back to its unpromoted side

label.ja: 相手の駒があるマスへ…
label.en: Move onto a square holding an enemy piece…

label.ja: 表を向けて自分の持駒に
label.en: …it goes to your hand, turned face up

title.ja: 持駒の角はどの空きマスにも打てる
title.en: A bishop in hand can be dropped on any empty square

explain.ja: もともと相手の駒だったものを自分の駒として使え、しかもどこにでも置けます。持駒は常に表向きで扱うので、敵陣に打っても成駒にはならない点に注意が必要です。
explain.en: A piece that was originally the opponent's becomes yours and can be dropped anywhere. Pieces in hand are always used face up, so dropping one in the enemy camp does not make it promoted; keep this in mind.

section.ja: 持駒はいつでも好きな場所に打てる!
section.en: Pieces in hand can be dropped anywhere at any time!

title.ja: 敵陣に持駒を打つ時も、表向きに
title.en: Pieces dropped in the enemy camp also go face up

explain.ja: 成駒を取っても、持ち駒としては元の生駒に戻ります。たとえば「と金」を取っても、使うときは歩兵になります。また、相手の玉を取れる手を「王手」と言い、持ち駒を玉の近くに打って王手するのもルール上問題ありません。ただし持ち駒の歩にはいくつか反則があります。
explain.en: Capturing a promoted piece gives you the original unpromoted piece in hand; capturing a tokin, for example, gives you a pawn. A move that threatens to capture the opponent's king is called check (王手), and dropping a piece in hand next to the king to give check is perfectly legal. However, dropping pawns is subject to several prohibitions.

section.ja: 持駒を敵陣に打つときも、裏返さない!表のまま使う
section.en: Do not flip pieces in hand when dropping them in the enemy camp! Use them face up

label.ja: 敵陣に持駒を打つ時も成駒にしてはいけない
label.en: Drops in the enemy camp cannot be promoted

label.ja: 持駒を打つ時は常に表向きで

title.en: Giving check with a piece in hand is OK

explain.ja: 持ち駒の枚数に制限はなく、取れるだけ取って好きなタイミングと場所に打てます。自分の駒は取れず、自分の駒がいるマスには動けません。打つときの反則は3つです。二歩は同じ筋に自分の歩が2枚並ぶように打つこと、打ち歩詰めは持ち駒の歩を打って玉を詰ませること(盤上の歩を動かして詰ますのは可)、行き所のない駒は動けるマスのない場所に打つことで、たとえば歩や香車を一段目に打つのは反則です。二歩が最も多い反則です。持ち駒の活用では、銀や桂馬は攻めの持ち駒として強く、金は玉が危ないとき玉の近くに打って守る基本的な受けになります。歩の持ち駒も、相手の利きを止めたり駒を誘い出したりと非常に便利です。
explain.en: There is no limit on pieces in hand; capture as much as you like and drop whenever and wherever you wish, but you cannot capture your own pieces or move onto their squares. Three drops are illegal: nifu (two of your unpromoted pawns on one file), uchifuzume (dropping a pawn to give checkmate; mating by moving a pawn on the board is fine), and a piece with no legal move afterwards, such as a pawn or lance dropped on the last rank. Nifu is the most common foul. For using pieces in hand, silver and knight are strong attacking drops, while a gold dropped beside the king is a basic defence when it is in danger. A pawn in hand is also very handy for blocking an enemy piece's line or luring pieces out.

section.ja: 持駒でいきなり王手してもOK
section.en: You can give check immediately with a piece in hand

label.ja: 持駒でいきなり王手してもOK
label.en: A drop may give check immediately
